source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 142: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions (variant 142): treat the initialization hang as an unproven symptom, and do not infer a platform-specific cause. Use an authorized disposable allocation, a finite watchdog, redacted logs, and automatic cleanup of child processes and temporary state. Record backend, launcher, library/driver versions, scheduler/container, world size and placement, fabric, selected interface, topology, and the exact stage where progress stops; label each item measured, estimated, or unknown. Do not alter production settings until a reversible canary is justified.

Baseline and membership checks: assign a run ID and capture for every rank its host, global/local rank, PID, expected/observed membership, device mapping, GPU/NIC identifiers, software/configuration hashes, rendezvous/store parameters (with secrets and endpoints redacted), process-group and collective entry/exit timestamps, last-progress time, backend debug output, interface/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall state, peer access, PCIe/NVLink topology, container device/shared-memory visibility, ulimits, and clock synchronization. Verify one process per expected rank, identical world size/rendezvous parameters and collective ordering, reachable peers, and no hidden rank or duplicate.

Falsifiable hypothesis: rank 6 is failing to reach the rendezvous or is selecting an unusable interface, so its peers wait in collective initialization. This predicts a rank-specific missing rendezvous/entry timestamp or failed path/interface evidence, and that replacing only the authorized interface/path choice or fixing the demonstrated membership mismatch makes a minimal all-reduce complete without changing code. Falsify it if all ranks enter with matching parameters and the same reachable path, or if the failure persists under a controlled known-good interface and reduced world.

Controlled experiment: first run a minimal, fixed-size all-reduce with a finite timeout and checksum/correctness check. Randomize repeated trials across matched single-node, reduced-world, and full-world placements while holding software, tensor size, launch order, and timeout constant; change one factor per comparison. Test interface selection only in an isolated canary, and collect per-rank outcomes. Separate denominators for rendezvous success, collective correctness/checksum, latency distribution, timeout/hang, rank failure, transport error, and cleanup; report units and confidence intervals where repetitions allow. Compare against competing explanations such as collective-order mismatch, wrong GPU visibility, topology/peer-access issue, network policy/MTU/firewall, resource exhaustion, container limits, or software incompatibility.

Decision and rollback: preserve the failing baseline, stop timed-out jobs, and roll back any diagnostic configuration when correctness, isolation, or bounded completion is not demonstrated. Escalate only with the redacted artifacts and exact reproduction; this plan identifies evidence to collect, not a confirmed root cause.

Use an authorized disposable allocation, a finite watchdog, redacted logs, and automatic cleanup of child processes and temporary state. Record backend, launcher, library/driver versions, scheduler/container, world size and placement, fabric, selected interface, topology, and the exact stage where progress stops; label each item measured, estimated, or unknown. Do not alter production settings until a reversible canary is justified.

Baseline and membership checks: assign a run ID and capture for every rank its host, global/local rank, PID, expected/observed membership, device mapping, GPU/NIC identifiers, software/configuration hashes, rendezvous/store parameters (with secrets and endpoints redacted), process-group and collective entry/exit timestamps, last-progress time, backend debug output, interface/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall state, peer access, PCIe/NVLink topology, container device/shared-memory visibility, ulimits, and clock synchronization. Verify one process per expected rank, identical world size/rendezvous parameters and collective ordering, reachable peers, and no hidden rank or duplicate.

Falsifiable hypothesis: rank 1 is failing to reach the rendezvous or is selecting an unusable interface, so its peers wait in collective initialization. This predicts a rank-specific missing rendezvous/entry timestamp or failed path/interface evidence, and that replacing only the authorized interface/path choice or fixing the demonstrated membership mismatch makes a minimal all-reduce complete without changing code. Falsify it if all ranks enter with matching parameters and the same reachable path, or if the failure persists under a controlled known-good interface and reduced world.

Controlled experiment: first run a minimal, fixed-size all-reduce with a finite timeout and checksum/correctness check. Randomize repeated trials across matched single-node, reduced-world, and full-world placements while holding software, tensor size, launch order, and timeout constant; change one factor per comparison. Test interface selection only in an isolated canary, and collect per-rank outcomes. Separate denominators for rendezvous success, collective correctness/checksum, latency distribution, timeout/hang, rank failure, transport error, and cleanup; report units and confidence intervals where repetitions allow. Compare against competing explanations such as collective-order mismatch, wrong GPU visibility, topology/peer-access issue, network policy/MTU/firewall, resource exhaustion, container limits, or software incompatibility.

Decision and rollback: preserve the failing baseline, stop timed-out jobs, and roll back any diagnostic configuration when correctness, isolation, or bounded completion is not demonstrated. Escalate only with the redacted artifacts and exact reproduction; this plan identifies evidence to collect, not a confirmed root cause.
risks: Root cause remains unproven without per-rank artifacts and domain review.
Timeout or interface/topology changes can mask rather than fix the fault.
Diagnostics may expose sensitive endpoints or identifiers and require redaction.
evidence_required: per-rank membership, rendezvous, ordering, timestamps, and backend logs
exact software, driver, launcher, topology, and configuration data
GPU/NIC/interface/container visibility and network-path checks
randomized matched trial outcomes with correctness, latency, timeout, failure, and cleanup denominators
domain-expert review
